name: empty-kernel-preserves-output-texture
no_effect: The entry's body is empty, so the texture keeps its authored texels. No input can do otherwise: with no body, nothing reaches a write, so the family has no computing variant.
rationale: The entry has an empty body and therefore preserves the complete poisoned write-only texture selection; the unused constant buffer and grid position satisfy its declared interface.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-eleven-2x1-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 11 and receives exact float4 zero from all ten linked _uber_clear bodies. A thirteen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The complete 2x1 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x1 resource.

name: manual-float4-fetch-at-an-offset-transformed-onto-three-of-four-pixels
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's manual-vertex-fetch case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero constants gave a degenerate position. Constant 132 enables manual fetch; table slot 0 holds the same-library callback re::vertexfetch::fetchFromFloat4, and record 0 of the vertex-argument buffer (15 records of 24 bytes, the rest null) points at float4 positions with stride 16 and offset 16, which skips a leading decoy vertex (40, 40, 40). The three positions are (-1, -1), (3, -1), (-1, 3) with z = 1/4 with the matrix z scale 2, so world z = 5/8. The instance matrix (objectToCrWorld, column-major) scales x and y by 1/2, scales z and translates by (-1/4, -1/4, 1/8); crWorldToProjArray[0] keeps x, y and w and maps z to z/2 + 1/16, so the clip triangle is (-3/4, -3/4), (5/4, -3/4), (-3/4, 5/4) at w = 1. It covers the pixel centres (-1/2, 1/2), (-1/2, -1/2) and (1/2, -1/2) of the 2x2 target with a margin of at least 1/4 from every edge and misses (1/2, 1/2): pixel (1, 0) keeps its fill. The depth is the same at all three vertices, so its interpolation is exact; every product and sum is a small dyadic value, exact in float with or without contraction, and the observer writes (x + 1/2, y + 1/2, z, 1) for each covered pixel. screenSpaceDepthBias = 1/4 adds 1/4 * w to clip z: depth 0.625. Constant 127 (PortalClippingMode) = 1 selects the portal clip distance: dot((world xyz, 1), portalPlane) with portalPlane = (0, 0, 1, -1/2) is 5/8 - 1/2 = 1/8 at every vertex, so the clip distance keeps the whole triangle (a wrong sign or operand would clip it away).

name: manual-vertex-fetch-null-buffer-defaults
no_effect: Zero instance and view constants give a degenerate position: the primitive covers no fragment, so the render target keeps its authored bytes.
rationale: Function constant 132 enables manual vertex fetch. Each of the fifteen VertexArgumentBuffer records is zero-initialized, so every embedded vertex-buffer pointer is null; the AIR helper branches around every visible-table lookup and supplies its defined default attribute. Slot zero carries the exact same-library invalid-format callback solely to give the table its structurally required float4(device uchar*) type; no callback is reachable. The only AIR loop exits when its unsigned 16-bit counter reaches 32. Zero instance/view constants produce a degenerate position, so the poisoned observation target remains deterministic. Buffer 30 and its reflected offset-zero device buffer are now authored explicitly; the invalid-format callback deterministically supplies the same default attribute when that first record is reached.

name: gather-mm-rhs-nt-bfloat-k40-two-experts
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-shape case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero extents stop the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 64 lanes (2 simdgroups) runs the single 16x64 output tile: B = 1, M = 16, N = 64, K = 40 (gemm_k_iterations_aligned = 2, remainder 8), no dimension declared aligned (user constant 0): the remainder and both whole blocks go through the guarded loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table. The indices select expert 0 for rows below 8 and expert 1 for the rest, so the kernel walks two row segments, each a full tile multiply over its expert (experts_stride_b = N*K = 2560), writing only its own rows. B[e][n][k] (ldb = 40): expert 0 holds q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the 64 column sums differ, and expert 1 holds q/2. A[m][k] (lda = 40): rows of segment 0 hold a = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating along k, rows of segment 1 hold 2a, so every row of the result is the same (2a . q/2 = a . q): the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 64 words observed (256 bytes) do not depend on write order, and a row given the other segment's expert would write another. Every input is a multiple of 0.5 at most 15, exact in bfloat; every product is a multiple of 0.5 at most 75 and every sum of 40 at most 3000, below 2^12: exact in float in any order or contraction. Every loop is finite by these inputs: the row-segment scan stops at M = 16, the K loop runs gemm_k_iterations_aligned = 2 times, the segment loop ends after the two segments, and the element loops have constant trip counts.

name: gather-mm-rhs-nt-bfloat-zero-shape
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: The nt bfloat counterpart of the committed mps_gather_mm_rhs_nn_half case (DESIGN D272): mps_gather_mm_rhs_nt_bfloat with the same function constants, resources, one-thread dispatch, and linked visible function (postfixPrimary_f). Its zero extents keep every loop bound finite, so the case observes the four-byte destination allocation; the kernel links translation units each with its own static initializer and no llvm.global_ctors list, and calls matmul2d, so its translation exercises the unordered-initializer rule (D272.4) and the matmul2d lowering (D272.3). Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: visible-table-clear-slot-two-2x2-output
rationale: One invocation takes the non-empty path because the authored bounds are float2(1), calls visible-function-table slot 2, and receives exact float4 zero from the linked _uber_clear body without dereferencing callback arguments. This entry writes a 2x2 block at primary-texture origin (2,0); the 4x2 poisoned resource contains that full footprint, which is selected for byte-exact comparison.

name: linked-single-fft-temp-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded FFT work item with unit extents and strides. The destination-temp path confines writes to the authored output allocation. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert. The authored threadgroup allocation bounds the combined-radix scratch footprint.

name: storage-level-counts-and-a-size-at-a-level
rationale: One thread stores (t.get_num_mip_levels(), t.get_width(lod), t.get_height(lod), c.get_num_mip_levels()) for a write-only 8x4 rgba32_float texture t and a write-only 2x2 rgba16_float cube c (neither is written) to device buffer 1. A storage texture's level count is the count the binder pushes, and t's size at a level reads that level's view (DESIGN D230). lod = 0 from constant buffer 0, a level of the texture, so every query is defined: out = (1, 8, 4, 1), each lane distinct from the 0xab initial bytes. The AIR has no loop.

name: direct-equalize-with-authored-linkage

name: sample-a-cube-with-explicit-gradients-through-a-sampler-held-beside-it-in-an-argument-buffer
rationale: DESIGN D285.21: constant argument buffer 0 is CubeMaterial {texturecube<float> t; sampler s;}, and the sampler is the case's own sampler state (normalized, minifies linearly, magnifies nearest, not mipmapped, clamp to edge), which the Metal oracle encodes into field 8 and the engine reads from the set-1 sampler array of the cube-gradient use. t is a 2x2 rgba16_float cube whose face f has texel (x, y) = (16(x + 2y), 16x, 16y, 16(f + 1)), a linear function of the texel on each face. Thread g samples t on its +x face at the direction (1, h, h), h = 0.25 for g < 2 and -0.25 otherwise, which is the face point s = t = 0.375 or 0.625, the texel-space point 0.75 or 1.25 on both axes, away from every face edge. An even g passes zero gradients, which magnify: the nearest texel, (0, 0) or (1, 1). An odd g passes dP/dx = (0, 0, 4) and dP/dy = (0, 4, 0), a footprint of four texels on the 2x2 face (a level of detail near 2, far from the magnification boundary at 0), which minifies: the bilinear sample, the face's linear function at 0.25 or 0.75 on both axes, its two texels weighed 3/4 and 1/4 on each axis, exact at any subtexel precision. Buffer 1 holds (0, 0, 0, 16), (12, 4, 4, 16), (48, 16, 16, 16), (36, 12, 12, 16), every value exact in half and float. A gradient that does not reach the sample, a sampler that does not reach it, or another face gives other bytes.

name: half-conversion-of-8-bit-srgb-and-16-bit-unorm-formats-by-read-and-sample
rationale: TODO 6.6's probe (DESIGN D351 item 5): how Metal converts the texels of formats no case bound before to a half result. Four 16x16 textures, each read as texture2d<half>: bgra8_unorm_srgb, r8_unorm_srgb and rg8_unorm_srgb with every code once per channel, and rg16_unorm codes: 0, 65535, codes whose c / 65535 lies nearest a tie between two adjacent half values (and their neighbours), and seeded codes. Lane i (of 256) takes texel (i mod 16, i div 16) at its centre (even i) or offset by a seeded fraction below one half (odd i; f8f81b81's coordinates): read at the coordinate truncated to the texel, sampled through a nearest and a linear clamp-to-edge sampler with pixel coordinates. Lane i writes its twelve results widened to float to out[12i..12i+11] of buffer 1 (per texture: read, nearest, linear), pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: half-conversion-of-half-float-and-signed-normalized-texels
rationale: How Metal converts half-float and signed normalized texels to half when a half texture reads or samples them, outside the bicubic filter (the formats half-conversion-of-wider-texels-by-read-and-sample does not bind). Four 16x16 textures: rgba16_float whose rows pair adjacent halves (texel 2m+1 one ulp above texel 2m, so a sample at the pair's midpoint sums to a rounding tie) with rows 3, 7, 11 and 15 of specials (signed zeros, infinities, NaN, the largest half, subnormals); rgba8_snorm with every code once per channel; rgba16_snorm codes whose c/32767 lies nearest a half tie, the ends (-32768, -32767) and random codes; rgba16_float in the subnormal range and just above it. Lane i takes texel (i mod 16, i div 16): at its centre (i mod 4 = 0), offset by seeded fractions k/256 (i mod 4 = 1), at the midpoint between it and its right neighbour (i mod 4 = 2), or at the centre of its 2x2 block (i mod 4 = 3): read at the coordinate truncated to the texel, sampled through a nearest and a linear clamp-to-edge sampler with pixel coordinates. Lane i writes its twelve results widened to float to out[12i..12i+11] of buffer 1 (per texture: read, nearest, linear), pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: loads-and-stores-past-a-device-buffer
rationale: Eight threads (DESIGN D225, the storage buffer form). idx = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 17, 63, 8, 9, 10, 11, 16, 17, 40, 79. Thread t loads src[idx[t]] into out[t]: threads 0 to 3 load src's four words, threads 4 to 7 load words 4 to 63, past src's 16 bytes (within its 256-byte reach), whose results Metal leaves undefined: out bytes 16 to 31 are the declared out-of-bounds reads of src. Thread t stores 0xA0000000 | t to out[idx[8 + t]]: threads 0 to 3 to out[8..12], threads 4 to 7 to words 16 to 79, past out's 64 bytes (within its 256-byte reach). So out = src[0..4], the four reads, 0xA0000000 to 0xA0000003, and four words of the initial 0xab bytes; nothing outside src and out changes.

name: sobel-two-pixels-whose-gradients-are-three-four-and-six-eight
rationale: The kernel writes two adjacent pixels from twelve taps of one sampled texture, all at the same pixel coordinate with twelve distinct texel offsets. Params place the sample origin at (1,1) of a 4x3 source, so every tap lands inside and the clamp mode never decides anything; the runtime sampler is unnormalized and nearest, so a tap returns exactly the texel it names. The output is R32Float, so only the red channel is observable, and the red plane is chosen so both gradients come out as small integers: the first pixel is Gx=3, Gy=4 and the second Gx=6, Gy=8. Every product on the way is exact - the only multiplies are by two and the two squarings of 3, 4, 6 and 8 - so the fmul/fadd pairs give the same answer whether or not they contract into fma, and the sums 25 and 100 are perfect squares. A Metal probe first confirmed that fast::sqrt is bit-identical to precise::sqrt on this hardware, so nothing here rests on which variant the lowering picks. The two texels must read back exactly 5 and 10.

name: select-the-acos-arm-of-the-unary-op-table-over-eight-inputs
rationale: The entry dispatches on a runtime `ArithmeticUnaryOp` read from its params buffer, so one dispatch exercises exactly one arm; this case sets it to 9, which is `air.acos.f32`. Eight inputs run through it and two more threads sit past `count` = 8, so the last two output floats must keep their 0xCC poison and show the signed guard held. The activation type is 0, which is the one value that skips the second helper entirely, so nothing but the unary call stands between the input and the store. 1 of the eight inputs have an exactly representable answer and are hand-certain anchors; every remaining value was derived independently in double precision and rounded, and Metal agrees with that derivation to within 1 unit(s) in the last place -- so the vector is pinned, not merely recorded. The inputs were also chosen from the set on which Metal's math library and the one MoltenVK's runtime compiler selects return the identical float: roughly half of the ordinary arguments to this function differ between them by one to three units in the last place, and negative zero is not preserved through the odd members of the family at all, so an exact comparison can only speak where the two libraries do.

name: fast-tangent-arctangent-and-arcsine-at-thirty-six-points
rationale:
The three largest uncovered air.* families in the corpus after the visible-function tables: air.fast_tan.f32 in 29 sources, air.fast_atan.f32 in 26 and air.fast_asin.f32 in 11, and no authored case for any of them. A prior session recorded them as blocked because the PRECISE members of this family diverge on MoltenVK by 1-3 ULP; the fast members do not, and all 36 lanes here reproduce bit for bit. That is the expected outcome rather than a lucky one -- SPIRV-Cross reaches Metal's own fast:: variant for an f32 operand, so both backends are running the same builtin, and the 1-2 ULP spread below is what proves the case is measuring an approximate function and not an accident of small exact arguments.

Every word was derived independently in float64 and rounded to float32 before the GPU was asked. Fifteen lanes are 0 ULP from that derivation -- tan(+-1), tan(2), tan(0.125), tan(1.5), atan(4), atan(0.75), asin(0), asin(+-1), asin(+-0.5), asin(0.125), asin(0.9) and the three zeros -- and no lane is more than 2 ULP away, so a lowering that answered a DIFFERENT function would be visible immediately rather than hidden inside a tolerance.

The inputs are chosen so each family identifies itself. All three functions are odd and each carries at least two +-pairs, so a lowering that lost the sign is caught. tan(2) is negative (-2.185) and tan(1.5) is 14.1, which is the pole side of pi/2: a lowering that clamped or took a magnitude answers neither. atan(100) is 1.5608, just under pi/2, which pins the asymptote and separates atan from a bare reciprocal or from asin. asin(+-1) is exactly +-pi/2, the domain edge, and is bit-identical to the constant 0x3fc90fdb, while asin(1) and atan(1) and tan(1) are 1.5708, 0.7854 and 1.5574 -- three different answers to the same argument, so the three symbols cannot be crossed without the case failing.

The 37th word is left at the 0xABABABAB fill and read back, so a write past the 36 the kernel owns is visible rather than silent.

name: log2-pass-parity-selects-the-primary-order
rationale: The only thing this kernel computes is a merge-sort pass count, and the whole count is two air.fast_log2.f32 calls: passes = max(1, uint(fast_ceil(fast_log2(count)) - fast_log2(groupSize)) + 1), and its LOW BIT alone selects which of the two index buffers every thread copies from. count is 1024 and threads_per_threadgroup is 8, so both logarithms land on exact powers of two -- log2(1024) = 10 and log2(8) = 3 are the two values a binary logarithm represents without rounding -- and the difference is exactly 7.0 whatever precision the fast variant carries. passes is 8, which is even, so all eight threads read `indices` and the output is 0xA0000000..0xA0000007. Choosing a base-two-exact pair is what makes the answer a fixed integer rather than a tolerance: a natural logarithm in place of log2 would give uint(ceil(6.93) - 1.386) + 1 = 6, still even and indistinguishable, so the companion case `log2-pass-parity-selects-the-scratch-order` runs the same shader at groupSize 4, where log2 answers 9 (odd, scratch) and ln answers 6 (even, primary). The pair pins the base, and each case alone pins the parity. The dispatch is one full threadgroup, count exceeds every thread's grid position, so no thread takes the early return, and the kernel contains no loop.

name: log2-pass-parity-selects-the-scratch-order
rationale: The odd arm of the pass-count parity that `log2-pass-parity-selects-the-primary-order` pins even, on the same shader and the same exact-logarithm inputs. count is 1024 and threads_per_threadgroup is 4, so air.fast_log2.f32 is asked only for log2(1024) = 10 and log2(4) = 2, both exact in binary, and passes = max(1, uint(10 - 2) + 1) = 9. Nine is odd, so every thread copies from `indicesTmp` instead of `indices` and the output is 0xB0000000..0xB0000003. This is also where the base of the logarithm becomes observable: a natural log would give uint(ceil(6.93) - 1.386) + 1 = 6 and select `indices`, so the two buffers hold disjoint value ranges and the recorded bytes say which function ran. The dispatch is one full threadgroup of four, count exceeds every grid position so no thread takes the early return, and the kernel is loop-free.

name: compact-the-one-line-the-delete-map-keeps-into-slot-zero
rationale: A stream-compaction kernel: each thread reads its delete flag, and a thread whose flag is zero atomically claims the next output slot and copies one ushort4 line record into it. The ushort4 load is the shape passes::access::vector_subword::direct_scalar_or_vector_width keys on -- the reflected footprint shows it split into two 4-byte strided accesses -- and no authored case reached that rule; this is the smallest of its eleven corpus hosts at 116 lines. The atomic makes slot assignment order-dependent in general, so the case is arranged so exactly ONE thread claims a slot: the delete map is 1,1,0,1 over a four-thread grid, so thread 2 alone reaches the atomic, takes slot 0, and lands line record 2 at destination byte 4 -- the emitter's own base is `&((ushort4*)dst)[0][2]`, four bytes in, so the record is written at an offset that is not a multiple of its own eight-byte size. Every other destination byte must stay 0xAA. The line-count buffer holds 4 and the kernel masks it to sixteen bits, so all four threads pass the bound; params.maxLines is 8, so the claimed slot is in range and the compensating atomic decrement is not taken. Every params byte except the four at offset 24 is 0xCC, which the reflected footprint says is exactly the range the kernel reads.

name: single-pixel-vertical-convolution-bias
rationale: One invocation passes the authored one-pixel destination bounds, samples a clamped zero source through the explicit pixel-coordinate sampler, applies zero three-tap weights and a float bias of one, and replaces the poisoned scalar output texel with exactly 1.0.

name: prune-pairings-broadcast-the-last-lane-index-to-every-pair
rationale: Every lane of one full simdgroup enters the loop with the same range, so the simdgroup is converged for both simd calls. hit_tests is one only at lanes 8 through 11, which makes the exclusive prefix sum zero for lanes 0-8, then 1, 2, 3, and four from lane 12 on; the running total never exceeds four, so the lane the broadcast names is always inside the simdgroup. The broadcast value is threads_per_simdgroup - 1, which every lane computes identically, so the result is 31 whichever lane it reads - and that 31 is what lands in the y half of every pair. The loop then exits because lane + 32 is never below 31. The 32 pairs must read back as (0,31).

name: prune-pairings-compact-four-hits-into-the-first-four-slots
rationale: Same inputs as the paired range case; this one captures the compaction instead. hit_tests is one only at lanes 8 through 11, so exactly those four lanes store, and they store to slots 0-3 taken from the exclusive prefix sum while reading slots 8-11. Source and destination sets are disjoint, so the four stores do not race with the four loads. The first four entries must become 108, 109, 110, 111 and the remaining twenty-eight must be untouched.

name: quad-lane-reduction-of-spatial-variance
rationale: One threadgroup of eight threads is exactly two quadgroups, so air.quadgroups_per_threadgroup is 2, air.quadgroup_index_in_threadgroup is 0 or 1, and air.thread_index_in_quadgroup runs 0..3 inside each. log2BlockSize 3 and a 16x4 subframe give every thread a 2x4 tile of the luma texture and make (extent.y - blockPos.y) >> 3 zero, so the 8x8 prefix-sum loop is skipped and each thread's sumSquare is exactly the sum of squares over its own eight texels. Thread t reads the constant value 2*(t+1), so its sumVar = (8*(2t+2)^2 + 32 + 8) >> 6 is 1, 2, 5, 8, 13, 18, 25, 32. air.quad_shuffle_down reduces each quad into sumVarLocal[quadID] under the quad-lane-zero predicate (16 and 88), the second reduction pass adds the two quads, and the single thread whose quad lane and quad index are both zero stores 104. Every value is an exact integer, so the observation depends on the lane index, the quad index, the quad count and the quad shuffle all agreeing, and on no rounding.

name: two-stores-around-a-device-scope-fence
rationale: Eight threads store in[t] + 1 to out[t], fence device memory with seq_cst ordering at device scope (barrier.fence, DESIGN D213), and store 2 in[t] to out[t + 8]. in[t] = 3t + 5, so out = (6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 10, 16, 22, 28, 34, 40, 46, 52). Each thread writes only its own words, so the fence orders nothing another thread observes: the case shows only that the fence lowers and leaves both stores. The AIR has no loop.

name: linked-single-unit-average-tgmem-tmp-output
rationale: Every source, destination, kernel, stride, dilation, threadgroup cube, and group-count extent is exactly one with zero offsets. The required multi-destination constants declare one float source at table element zero and one active float destination at element one, so the small-parameter average path executes only its unit window and bounded single invocation before writing exact one.

name: linked-single-threadgroup-zero-bin
rationale: One 1x1 threadgroup dispatches one invocation. kLogBinEntries=0 makes both initialization and flush loops contain exactly one bin, kTGSizeIs256=false uses the literal one-thread group size as their stride, and source_size=1x1 bounds the image path. The exact linked callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing resources; the poisoned global bin makes the local-atomic aggregation observable byte-exactly.
